text:
marta (solutions): Hey team — Jordan from NovaHealth wants to run a 2-week POC. They need hosted API keys + a small dedicated pool for burst testing. Also asking for billing visibility and a hard spend cap. Can someone own provisioning?

alex (sales): I can coordinate. Jordan — can you confirm expected avg qps and peak token/day so we can size the pool and set the quota? Also do you need VPC/private deployment or just hosted keys for now?

jordan (customer): Thanks, Alex. For first phase: ~5 qps average, 20 qps peak. Tokens ~1.2M/day peak. We only need hosted keys initially. If the POC goes well, we'll talk dedicated + VPC.

marta (solutions): Perfect. For hosted POC we typically create a billing project with: (1) trial credits (50k tokens) + (2) per-day hard spend cap, and (3) ephemeral API keys for engineers. Do we need multiple teams to be split into sub-projects?

jordan (customer): One project is fine. Engineers will use ephemeral keys; product and infra will need audit logs.

sam (eng-infra): @marta @alex I can create the billing project and enable ephemeral key flow. Need these from Jordan: billing email, preferred org name, and the spend cap value. Also confirm whether we should enable rate limiting at the project level.

jordan (customer): billing@novahealth.com; org name: NovaHealth-POC; set a hard spend cap to $500 for the 2-week pilot. Rate limiting OK at 50 rps project-wide (they won't hit that).

amelyn (note: not a participant)

alex (sales): Got it. @sam can you do the provisioning steps and tag the project with `poc:novahealth` and `poctype:hosted`? Also please add audit log retention of 30 days.

sam (eng-infra): On it. Workflow I'll run: 1) create billing project `redwood-poc-novahealth` 2) allocate trial credits 50k tokens 3) set spend_cap_usd=500 4) enable ephemeral keys + audit logs 30d 5) add project-level rate limit 50rps 6) create initial API key for integration test (label `integration/temp`).

infra-bot: Billing project created: `redwood-poc-novahealth` (id: proj_01GfXk). Trial credits: 50,000 tokens. Spend cap: $500. Owner: sam.

marta (solutions): Thanks @sam — can you also enable cost alerts to slack channel #sales? Thresholds at 50%, 80%, 95% of spend cap.

sam (eng-infra): Done. Alerts posted to #sales and sent to jordan@novahealth.com. Also created ephemeral key runbook for their team: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/poc-ephemeral-keys (internal link).

jordan (customer): Great, I logged in and tested the temp key — streaming responses look good. Quick Q: are there any limits on model selection for hosted POC? We want to test both redwood-4x and a quantized cheaper variant.

amartA (note: not a participant)

marta (solutions): For hosted we support both. We'll pin the default to `redwood-4x` and allow fallback to `redwood-4x-quant` for cost fatigue. I updated the POC config: `preferred_models: ["redwood-4x", "redwood-4x-quant"]` and set fallback policy `auto-fallback: enabled` if latency spikes or cost > threshold.

sam (eng-infra): One operational note: because token usage could spike, I added a temporary dedicated burst pool rule that allows them to burst to a single small GPU instance for 30 minutes every 6 hours, capped to $200 of the spend cap. This won't provision a full dedicated tenant but helps simulate scale without full Dedicated onboarding.

jordan (customer): That's perfect — gives us the burst headroom we need. Anything else we should know?

amartA (note: not a participant)

marta (solutions): Next steps: Alex to run kickoff with Jordan tomorrow, Sam to handover runbook & keys, infra-bot will post daily usage summary. Alex — can you confirm kickoff time?

alex (sales): Scheduling for tomorrow 11am PT. Invites sent. Jordan, we also included a short security questionnaire response bundle in the invite (answers about data retention, KMS options, SOC2 artifacts).

jordan (customer): Received. Thanks everyone, excited to get started. :rocket:

infra-bot: Daily usage summary will post at 08:00 UTC. Current spend: $0.00. Remaining cap: $500.
